Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

meta5number 0.3.0

  • Any set of reported quantiles. The new function reporting_scenario() describes what a study reports by the probabilities of its sample quantiles, with or without the minimum and the maximum, for example reporting_scenario(c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)) for the median with the 5th and 95th percentiles. Its result is passed as the argument scenario of se_imputed(), c_mu(), c_sigma(), inflation_factors(), estimator_weights() and imputed_moments(), which compute the BLUE from these reported values and its exact factors at every sample size that is at least the number of reported values. The named scenarios "S1" to "S5" are special cases and give the results they gave before.

  • A quantile definition of your own. The argument type takes, besides the nine definitions of quantile(), a function of the probabilities p and the sample size n that returns the ranks r and the weights gamma of the rule (1 - gamma) x[r] + gamma x[r + 1]. The help of se_imputed() and Appendix C of the vignette write Tukey’s hinges, the quartiles of fivenum(), as such a rule.

  • The print of se_imputed() names a reporting_scenario() by its reported values and a rule by “a user-supplied quantile rule”.

  • imputed_moments() checks the length of the weights given as w_mean and w_sd, and c_mu_shortcut() and c_sigma_shortcut() say that the shortcut formulas exist for the scenarios S1 to S3 when they are given another scenario.

  • The paper of the engine, Wu and Tong (2026), is cited as arXiv:2611.19980 (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.19980), where it was cited as a manuscript, and orderStatMoments at its version 0.3.1.

  • The results for the scenarios "S1" to "S5" and the quantile definitions 1 to 9 are those of 0.2.1.

meta5number 0.2.1

  • This version corrects a defect that meta5number 0.2.0 has when it runs with version 0.3.0 of orderStatMoments, and it replaces 0.2.0. The functions that take a precomputed moments object (c_mu(), c_sigma(), imputed_moments() and estimator_weights()) check that the object holds the moments of the standard normal order statistics. Since its version 0.3.0, orderStatMoments stores the constants a and b of a distribution a + bZ in the component affine, where it stored them in location and scale before, and the check of 0.2.0 read the former names. With orderStatMoments 0.3.0 the check was therefore skipped: an object computed with mean, sd, os_shift or os_multiplier away from their defaults was accepted without a message, and results computed from it were wrong (the factor that c_mu() returns, for example). The check now reads affine, and it stops when an object of orderStatMoments does not carry that component. A call without moments, or with the object of the standard normal, was not affected, and its results are unchanged.

  • The package requires orderStatMoments 0.3.0 or later (Imports: orderStatMoments (>= 0.3.0)). Update it with remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/orderStatMoments").

  • The references cite orderStatMoments at its version 0.3.0, and its paper by the title it has now, “orderStatMoments: Exact Means, Variances, and Covariances of Order Statistics in R”.

meta5number 0.2.0

  • The engine of the exact moments is now the package orderStatMoments, renamed from osmoments, and every call and the Imports field follow it. Install it with remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/orderStatMoments").

  • The package is renamed meta5number (it was fivenumMeta in 0.1.0), so that the name says what it is for: meta-analysis from five-number summaries. The functions, their arguments and their results are unchanged. library(meta5number) replaces library(fivenumMeta), and the old installation should be removed first (remove.packages("fivenumMeta")).

  • The constants of the shortcut formulas c_mu_shortcut() and c_sigma_shortcut() carry two decimals, as Table 3 of the paper and its supplement table print them since the refit on the paper’s grid of 40 sample sizes (n = 901 added). The anchors keep four decimals, since they are the limits of the paper’s Theorem 1. The documented errors were recomputed and are of the same size as before (at most 0.42% on the grid for the BLUE’s formulas). The constants of 0.1.0, for the record: BLUE, mean, S1 (2.006, -0.810), S2 (0.142), S3 (0.838, -0.576); SD, S1 (0.8278, 0.330, 1.2041), S2 (-0.863), S3 (5.267, -10.364, 8.327); Wan-Luo-Shi version, mean, S1 (2.006, -0.811), S2 (0.142), S3 (0.835, -0.572); SD, S1 (0.8705, 0.418, 1.2199), S2 (-0.845), S3 (5.191, -10.204, 8.525).

  • The test grid of test-exact-any-n.R has 40 sample sizes (n = 901 added).
